input.prompt:
Propose one experimentally testable VH/VL redesign for B7-H3 Arm A
parent 275, for a Y-shaped humanized IgG with separate HC and LC.
Use only the reference evidence below at its stated strength. Preserve the arm's
intended epitope and complete variable-domain framework. Treat reference-chain
and internal-coverage uncertainties explicitly. Nominate one conservative loop substitution to test against the unchanged parent. Treat modeled patch contacts as a basis for proposing an experiment. A speculative hypothesis is acceptable if its mechanistic rationale and uncertainty are explicit.
Return JSON with parent_id, arm, status, vh, vl, changes, rationale and uncertainties.
Do not use tools or read other files. The final Fc and pairing architecture are
outside this proposal. Do not represent predicted binding as measured.
Use the verified RFantibody design-loop positions to distinguish design loops
from framework. The AF3 contacts are model observations. Propose at most two
loop substitutions as hypotheses when supported by the parent evidence, with
explicit residue-level rationale. Preserve framework residues and sequence
lengths. If the input poses are insufficient, record why.

proposal.status: Proposed single-substitution hypothesis for experimental testing
proposal.rationale: VH S104 is within the verified RFantibody H3 design loop (positions 99–111). It is the only listed antibody residue that approaches the same target residue in both contact-positive AF3 samples. Its minimum distances to canonical B7-H3 residue 129 are 4.21 Å and 2.81 Å. Threonine retains the hydroxyl and adds a methyl group, giving a conservative test of whether local packing or hydroxyl orientation affects recognition at the intended IgV1 FG-loop patch. All parent framework residues and both variable-domain lengths are preserved. Compare S104T with unchanged parent 275 in matched Y-shaped humanized IgGs with separate HC and LC. Measure binding to native human 4Ig B7-H3 and compare their binding responses to the same FG-loop point mutants, with controls for antigen integrity, to test whether patch dependence is retained.
uncertainties: Two of four AF3 samples show no listed patch contacts, and the surrounding contacts differ between the two positive samples. The minimum distances do not identify the interacting atoms or establish a hydrogen bond. The poses support testing S104T, but leave its effect on binding and epitope retention unresolved.

The 8H9 record supports the FG-loop region at the lineage level. The supplied record identifies the H1L2 and H2L1 patent pairs and reports 34.8 nM binding to 4Ig for each. The Fab-only 5CMA structure leaves antigen-contact geometry unresolved, and the supplied evidence does not verify full mature VH/VL coverage, including possible internal gaps, or establish an exact sequence match between the crystallized chains and either tested humanized pair. No reference-chain residues were grafted.

The 8H8 parental mutant-binding result implicates canonical R127 without verifying the tested humanized HC/LC sequences or a contact for parent 275. Exact overlap with the T3CL11 co-crystal remains unresolved pending canonical residue mapping.
